chains.title: ATF3 gains binding on the non-risk C allele at an FTO intronic dELS

links.claim: ATF3 binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T: QBiC-SELEX with ATF3's own model gives z 21.73 and effect +1.403, with a strong site on both alleles (ref 98.9th, alt 99.7th percentile). ATF3 is expressed in adipose (57.63 TPM, rank 88/1631), but the only ENCODE ChIP peak over the variant is in HCT116, and no adipose ATF3 peak is reported; E04 also notes no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, so adipose occupancy is not proven. I chose ATF3 because it has an own-model QBiC alt-gain, strong site, and reasonably high adipose expression among the bound-elsewhere TFs.

The variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208, an active enhancer-like cCRE with co-factor/Pol II binding in ENCODE, so an allele-specific ATF3 site could alter enhancer output; however, the cCRE activity data are maxima over biosamples and are not adipose-specific.

The dELS is in the FTO intron, and FTO is the top Open Targets L2G gene (0.99) with a GTEx FTO eQTL in skeletal muscle (alt C NES +0.14); however, there is no significant adipose eQTL in GTEx v8, so FTO is the best-supported target but adipose target-gene direction is not established. IRX3 is not excluded as an alternative target.
Subcutaneous adipose/preadipocytes are the disease-relevant expression context; ATF3 is expressed there and the element is active, but matched adipose ATF3 occupancy is absent/unknown.

GWAS reports the T allele as the risk/effect allele for BMI and obesity. ATF3 binds C more than T, so risk T has weaker ATF3 binding; if ATF3 represses FTO at this element, risk T would derepress FTO, while if ATF3 activates FTO the direction would be opposite. The ATF3-to-FTO-to-obesity direction is therefore conditional, not demonstrated.

predictions: Allele-specific ATF3 CUT&RUN/ChIP in heterozygous preadipocytes will show stronger ATF3 occupancy on C than T at this base.
ATF3 knockdown/knockout will change FTO enhancer reporter activity or FTO expression in preadipocytes.
The risk T allele will have lower ATF3 occupancy; FTO expression direction will depend on whether ATF3 is repressive or activating at this element.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ATF3 CUT&RUN/ChIP in subcutaneous preadipocytes shows no C-over-T occupancy at this base.
ATF3 perturbation does not change FTO enhancer activity or FTO expression in preadipocytes.
A linked variant in the same dELS fully explains the adipose/GWAS signal and this base has no allelic effect.

chains.title: TEAD1 gains binding on the non-risk C allele at the FTO intronic dELS

links.claim: TEAD1 binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T: QBiC-SELEX with TEAD1's own model gives z 21.23 and effect +1.544, with a strong site on both alleles (98.8th percentile). TEAD1 is expressed in adipose (40.88 TPM, rank 148/1631), but the only ENCODE ChIP peak over the variant is in HepG2, not adipose; adipose occupancy is unproven.
The variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208, an active enhancer-like cCRE, so allele-specific TEAD1 binding could change enhancer activity; adipose-specific activity is not shown.

The dELS is in the FTO intron and FTO is the top L2G gene (0.99), with a skeletal-muscle FTO eQTL (alt C NES +0.14); no significant adipose eQTL is reported, and IRX3 remains an unexcluded alternative target.
Subcutaneous adipose/preadipocytes are the expression context; TEAD1 is expressed there, but matched adipose TEAD1 ChIP and adipose-specific enhancer activity are not demonstrated.

Risk T binds TEAD1 less than C. If TEAD1 is activating at this element, risk T would lower TEAD1-dependent FTO enhancer output; whether lower FTO in preadipocytes promotes obesity is not established, so the phenotype direction remains conditional.

TEAD1 knockdown will reduce FTO enhancer reporter activity if TEAD1 is activating at this element.
Risk T will show lower TEAD1 occupancy and, if TEAD1 is activating, lower FTO expression.

chains.title: JUN/AP-1 gains binding on the non-risk C allele at the FTO intronic dELS

links.claim: JUN binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T: QBiC-SELEX with JUN's own model gives z 17.91 and effect +0.317; the better-allele site strength rises from 82.8th percentile on ref to 99.8th on alt. JUN is very highly expressed in adipose (442.88 TPM, rank 3/1631), but the only ENCODE ChIP peak over the variant is in HepG2, not adipose; AP-1 family redundancy further weakens the specific JUN claim.
The variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208 within an active enhancer-like cCRE, so allele-specific JUN/AP-1 occupancy could alter enhancer output; the evidence is not adipose-specific.
The element is in the FTO intron; FTO has the strongest L2G support (0.99) and a skeletal-muscle eQTL (alt C NES +0.14), but no significant adipose eQTL is reported and IRX3 is not excluded.
Subcutaneous adipose/preadipocytes are the disease-relevant context; JUN is highly expressed there, but matched adipose ChIP and adipose-specific enhancer activity are absent.

Risk T has lower JUN binding than C. Because AP-1 can activate or repress, the direction of FTO change on risk T is not determined by the binding data; reduced AP-1 occupancy could shift FTO expression in preadipocytes, but the phenotype direction remains conditional.

Subcutaneous adipose/preadipocytes are the expression context; FOXP1 is expressed there at lower levels, but matched adipose ChIP and adipose-specific enhancer activity are missing.

Risk T binds FOXP1 more strongly than C. If FOXP1 acts as a repressor at this element, risk T would repress FTO more and lower FTO expression; the FOXP1-repressive-to-obesity direction is not demonstrated, so the phenotype link is conditional.
